page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-64 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier capabilities, particularly in CPU-bound tasks. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2545.0 and a multi-core score of 24713.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. It demonstrates strong memory bandwidth, reaching 203.88 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 127.63 GB/sec for write operations. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform highly, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 37.19 GB/sec and Passmark CPU extended instructions testing scoring 112137.73.

Given its high compute-to-memory ratio and lack of bundled local storage, the n4d-highcpu-64 is highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local SSDs. It is well-suited for software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and text processing. It also supports moderate-scale database operations and small-to-medium LLM inference tasks, processing 196.81 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B parameter model.
